title: DeepSeek to Raise at Least $12 Billion in Tencent-Backed Funding
source_used: The Edge Malaysia (carries Bloomberg's own article text, https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/820698); Reuters version on The Economic Times; Investing.com on Yahoo Finance. Bloomberg page itself blocked (HTTP 403).
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 6 Oct 2026, citing people familiar, that DeepSeek is close to securing at least 80 billion yuan (about US$12 billion) in its latest funding round.
Battery maker CATL and Tencent have committed among the largest amounts; the round closes soon, but details may still change in final talks.

DeepSeek first sought about 50 billion yuan; interest outstripped expectations after the successful release of its latest AI model, and based on term sheets signed the final tally could approach 100 billion yuan.
DeepSeek had originally targeted a valuation of about 500 billion yuan; the previous 50-billion-yuan round valued it at roughly 350 billion yuan.
Once the round closes, the next step is to restructure the company to prepare for an IPO, expected in early 2027.
Tencent made the biggest investment in the previous round, 10 billion yuan; DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 of Huawei's top AI accelerators at a data center in Inner Mongolia.
The raise was briefly suspended after comments widely attributed to founder Liang Wenfeng about US-China AI competition went viral (Yicai reported in July).
Reuters could not immediately verify the report; DeepSeek, Tencent and CATL did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
quote_evidence: DeepSeek is close to securing at least 80 billion yuan (US$12 billion) in its latest round of funding, blowing past its own capital-raising target ahead of a landmark initial public offering in early 2027.
While discussions around the current deal near an end, details may still change in final talks, the people said.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
why_it_matters_hint: One of China's best-known AI labs is raising far more than it first planned, with Tencent and CATL as large backers, ahead of an expected 2027 listing.
notes: Bloomberg's page could not be opened; the full Bloomberg text was read on The Edge Malaysia and cross-checked against the Reuters version on The Economic Times (80 billion yuan = $11.93 billion). Sources are unnamed; DeepSeek, Tencent and CATL had not commented.
